stories.headline: Big B mourns Nepal flood devastation, says it is unbearable to watch
stories.title: Big B mourns Nepal flood devastation, says it is unbearable to watch
stories.summary: Mumbai, Aug 29 : Megastar Amitabh Bachchan expressed his concern over the devastating floods in Nepal, describing the destruction as “unbearable to watch”. Taking to his blog, Amitabh said that the fury of nature cannot be battled, but calls for divine intervention. Big B wrote on his blog: “On a more serious note the devastation of the floods in Nepal are unbearable to watch… the fury of nature can never be battled with .. its respect needs the presence of the divine…we pray .. for that in itself is beyond all…(sic).” It was on August 26 that Nepal suffered catastrophic flash floods. The Nepal's National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority said that the bodies of 579 people swept away by the floods had so far been recovered. In comparison, 1,924 people remained out of contact as of Friday evening. The actor also shared a picture of his wrist filled with rakhis on the occasion of Raksha Bandhan. “...may this bond of love, affection and care live eternally - the dedication of the relation between a sister and a brother, never to be broken or forgotten... its sacred thread tied to the wrist, is the symbol of perpetuity in the relationship… its auspicious presence fortifies its reason…” Talking about work, Amitabh, the octogenarian, is currently keeping busy with the “Kalki 2898 AD” sequel, helmed by Nag Ashwin. The film is an epic mythological science fiction film that also stars Kamal Haasan, Prabhas, Deepika Padukone, and Disha Patani. The first installment is set in a dystopian future in the year 2898 AD in the city of Kashi, the story follows a group on a mission to protect lab subject SUM-80's unborn child, believed to be Kalki, the final incarnation of Vishnu. He will reportedly be seen in Nitesh Tiwary’s upcoming magnum opus “Ramayana: Part 1”, which also stars Ranbir Kapoor, Sai Pallavi, Yash, and Sunny Deol. The icon will reportedly play the character of Jatayu. Big B was last seen on screen in the action thriller film Vettaiyan, directed by T. J. Gnanavel. --IANS

stories.headline: 'Water up to 20 feet... climbed trees to stay alive': Indians rescued from flood-hit Nepal
stories.title: 'Water up to 20 feet... climbed trees to stay alive': Indians rescued from flood-hit Nepal
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: After the first batch of 106 stranded Maharashtra tourists reached India, people thanked the Indian and Nepalese authorities for facilitating the rescue.

New Delhi: People from different parts of the country, who were rescued from flood-ravaged Nepal, on Saturday recounted the extent of devastation in the Himalayan Nation and considered themselves lucky to have escaped the catastrophe.
Migrant labourers from Bihar's Bettiah referred to the flash floods as "unimaginable", while speaking to IANS in their hometown.
One of the labourers said, "There were five to seven of us, three of our people went missing...
There was a lot of water in the area, rising up to 20 feet.
We took our children and ran up the hill.
After an hour, when the water level receded, we went to look for them, but we could not find the three people."
"We were told to run away from there as people said there is no guarantee the water (flood) might come again," he added.
A youngster said, "At around 9:30 a.m., I heard a lot of noise.
I went outside to see what was happening, but I could only see dust.
Moments later, I saw that there was a lot of water due to the storm...
Immediately, I alerted the people inside.

stories.headline: Nepal flood horror reaches UP as 10 bodies recovered from Gandak river
stories.title: Nepal flood horror reaches UP as 10 bodies recovered from Gandak river
stories.summary: Nepal flood horror reaches UP as 10 bodies recovered from Gandak river
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Ten bodies were recovered from multiple locations across Uttar Pradesh, with police saying they were found in rivers carrying waters downstream from flood-hit Nepal.

The deadly Nepal floods have left a grim trail across the border, with 10 bodies recovered from rivers in Uttar Pradesh over the past two days, believed to have been swept downstream from the flood-hit neighbouring country, Reuters reported.
Six of the bodies were recovered from the Gandak river in Maharajganj and Kushinagar districts, both of which border Nepal, while authorities are yet to identify the deceased or trace their families.
In Maharajganj, three bodies, including those of two women, were recovered on Thursday after being spotted in the river’s strong current.
A Sashastra Seema Bal (SSB) rescue team monitoring the river and adjoining areas retrieved them using a motorboat and sent them to the district mortuary.
The Gandak enters India after flowing through Nepal as part of the Trishuli river system.
The Bhotekoshi river, which originates in Tibet, flows into the Trishuli before it eventually enters India as the Gandak, carrying the impact of the floods downstream.
Officials said the bodies were suspected to have been swept into Indian territory from Nepal.
Authorities are in touch with their Nepalese counterparts to establish whether the deceased were among those reported missing after the disaster and to trace their relatives.
In neighbouring Kushinagar, three more bodies were recovered from the Gandak on Friday.
They were spotted near barrage pier number 3 in the Madanpur-Sukrauli area of Khadda, prompting police and administrative officials to reach the spot.
Khadda SHO Sandeep Singh said SDRF monitoring teams spotted the bodies floating in the river and subsequently retrieved them.

article_sentences: Singer Vishal Mishra has pledged to hold concerts in Assam and Nepal, with every penny raised going towards flood relief and affected communities.

Mumbai: Musician Vishal Mishra has announced plans to organise concerts in Assam and Nepal, pledging that every penny raised from the events will go towards flood relief and supporting people affected by the disasters.
The singer-composer shared the announcement on Instagram, saying he was deeply affected by the devastation caused by the floods.
An official announcement on the concerts is expected soon.
“My heart is heavy seeing what's happening So I have made a decision.
I WILL PERFORM A CONCERT IN #NEPAL AND A CONCERT IN #ASSAM.
EVERY SINGLE PENNY.
WILL GO TOWARDS FLOOD RELIEF AND THE PEOPLE AFFECTED.
I GIVE YOU MY WORD.
Announcement soon (sic),” Vishal wrote.
He captioned the post: “Stay strong, will do whatever I can individually, Har Mahadev.”
The announcement comes as Assam and Nepal continue to grapple with the aftermath of devastating floods.

stories.headline: 'Strikes not just near LoC': Ex-Army chief on India's fresh tactics in Op Sindoor
stories.title: 'Strikes not just near LoC': Ex-Army chief on India's fresh tactics in Op Sindoor
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: NEW DELHI: Former Army chief General M Naravane on Saturday described Operation Sindoor as "very necessary action", stating that it marked a significant shift in India’s approach towards Pakistan.

Naravane said India moved beyond targeting terrorist bases along the border to striking their supporters and infrastructure deep inside Pakistan, signalling a more assertive response to cross-border terrorism.

Speaking to reporters in Vadodara after attending an event, Naravane, the 28th Chief of the Army Staff, said India’s earlier responses to terror attacks, including the Uri and Pulwama attacks, had largely focused on terrorist hideouts close to the border.
“Operation Sindoor, which took place after the Pahalgam attack, was a very necessary action...
Previously, whenever such attacks occurred, like after Uri, and Balakot strikes after Pulwama -- we were mostly targeting terrorist hideouts close to the border,” he said, news agency PTI reported.

“But this time, the strikes carried out targeted their supporters and those who provide them backing, wherever they may be -- not just near the Line of Control, but deep inside Pakistan, in Muridke and Bahawalpur, from where they receive this support,” he added.
Naravane said the operation sent a message that those supporting terrorism could not escape Indian action regardless of where they were located.
“As our defence minister Rajnath Singh had said, 'we will enter their territory and eliminate them', and there will be no protection for them.
So, this was a very significant shift in our modus operandi,” he said.

stories.headline: Operation Sindoor marked significant shift in India's approach towards Pak: ex-Army chief Naravane
stories.title: Operation Sindoor marked significant shift in India's approach towards Pak: ex-Army chief Naravane
stories.summary: Vadodara, Aug 29: Operation Sindoor marked a "very significant shift" in India's approach towards Pakistan as the strikes targeted not only terrorist hideouts near the border but also their supporters deep inside the neighbouring country, former Army chief General M M Naravane said on Saturday. Speaking to reporters after attending a private event in Vadodara to promote the start-up ecosystem, he said the operation, carried out following the Pahalgam terror attack a year ago, demonstrated that those providing support to terrorists could not escape Indian action regardless of where they were located. "Operation Sindoor, which took place after the Pahalgam attack, was a very necessary action," said Naravane, who had served as the 28th Chief of the Army Staff. Earlier, India's military response had largely been focused on terrorist hideouts located close to the border, he said, referring to earlier terror attacks, including in Uri and Pulwama. "Previously, whenever such attacks occurred -- like after Uri, and Balakot strikes after Pulwama -- we were mostly targeting terrorist hideouts close to the border. "But this time, the strikes carried out targeted their supporters and those who provide them backing, wherever they may be -- not just near the Line of Control, but deep inside Pakistan, in Muridke and Bahawalpur, from where they receive this support," said general Naravane (retd). He said India demonstrated that those providing support to terrorism "anywhere cannot escape". "As our Defence Minister Rajnath Singh had said, 'we will enter their territory and eliminate them', and there will be no protection for them. So, this was a very significant shift in our modus operandi," the former Army chief said. Asked about reports that Pakistan had become more active in the Sir Creek sector and was carrying out "Operation Ababil", general Naravane (retd) said such activities happen, adding that he did not have complete information about the reported operation. "These kinds of activities keep happening. I don't have complete information about this right now since I am retired," he said. However, Indian armed forces remained vigilant and would take appropriate action if required, he added. "I would like to say that whatever activity takes place, our forces always keep a close watch on it. There is nothing to panic about, and whatever action needs to be taken, appropriate action will be taken at the right time," the former Army chief said. Asked whether Pakistan was capable of taking on India, the former general said, "In my opinion, no." On India-China relations, general Naravane (retd) said the recent talks between National Security Advisor Ajit Doval and Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi should be viewed in the context of the long-standing boundary dispute between the two countries. He said the meeting was the 25th round of Special Representative-level talks and was not taking place for the first time. "This discussion that took place -- the 25th round of Special Representative-level talks between Ajit Doval from our side and Foreign Minister Wang Yi from China -- is not happening for the first time," he added. He said the key point to keep in mind is that there is a boundary dispute between India and China. "Exactly where the boundary lies has not been clearly demarcated either on maps or on the ground. It is because of this lack of demarcation that occasional disputes arise between India and China," the former Army chief added. On the proposed theatre commands, General Naravane (retd) said the discussion on theatreisation of the armed forces had begun after the Kargil War and that it was not a new concept. "The discussion on theaterisation first began after the Kargil War. It has already been 25 to 26 years since then. Theaterisation is not a new concept; it is a continuous process and an evolution," he said. The former Army chief further said there was broad agreement to establish theatre commands in India in view of rapidly changing modern warfare and shorter decision-making cycles. Everyone agrees that such theatre commands should be established in India as well, he said. "Considering the way the nature of modern warfare is transforming and decision cycles are becoming progressively shorter, it is essential that we move toward theaterisation as expeditiously as possible," the former Army chief said.

stories.headline: Karnataka CM Shivakumar to send Nagendra’s resignation to Governor
stories.title: Karnataka CM Shivakumar to send Nagendra’s resignation to Governor
stories.summary: Mysuru (Karnataka), Aug 29 : Karnataka Chief Minister, D.K. Shivakumar, on Saturday said he would send Minister for Planning and Statistics B. Nagendra’s resignation letter to Governor Thaawarchand Gehlot today, after the former minister resigned from the Cabinet amid a political controversy surrounding the alleged Valmiki Corporation scam. Addressing the media in Mysuru, CM Shivakumar said Nagendra had voluntarily tendered his resignation to prevent embarrassment to the Congress party and accused the BJP and JD(S) of focussing on politics instead of issues concerning the state and its people. "The man has come and voluntarily submitted his resignation to avoid embarrassment to the party. I am sending the resignation letter to the Governor today,” CM Shivakumar said. Reacting to the BJP and JD(S) moving ahead with a protest march, Shivakumar stated that the Opposition was more interested in politics than addressing issues such as drought and the Cauvery water dispute. “For them, politics is important. Drought and the lives of people are not important. They are not concerned about the welfare of the state. They do not want to discuss the Cauvery issue or how we are managing the drought,” he said. Shivakumar said he had asked the Opposition to submit a notice and come forward for a discussion in the Assembly, but alleged that they had instead focussed on the resignation of Nagendra. “I asked them to give a notice and come for a discussion. They only focussed on taking the sacrifice of an innocent person,” he said. Taking a swipe at the BJP and JD(S), Shivakumar alleged that the Opposition was unable to accept his becoming Chief Minister. “What they want is politics. They are not able to tolerate that I have become the Chief Minister. The whole NDA is not able to digest this fact. Let good happen to them,” he said. Meanwhile, senior BJP leader and former minister B. Sriramulu alleged the BJP was not responsible for Nagendra’s emotional distress and blamed the Congress party for his resignation. “We are not responsible for the tears of Minister Nagendra. The Congress party is responsible for your tears. BJP leaders are not responsible for your tears. The Congress is the root cause of your suffering,” Sriramulu claimed. Addressing Nagendra directly, Sriramulu said the former minister appeared restless and claimed that the alleged scam involving the Valmiki Corporation had continued to haunt him. “You are not in control. You are not able to sit in one place. Even during the Assembly session, I observed that you were always moving from one person to another and talking. Your karma has caught up with you,” he said. Sriramulu also referred to Chandrashekar, the Dalit officer who died by suicide, and said the incident and the grief of his family members were continuing to haunt Nagendra. “The tears of Chandrashekar’s family are following you like a curse and haunting you wherever you go. Because of this, your tears are coming,” he said. Responding to Nagendra’s challenge to BJP leaders in the region to face him in elections, BJP MLA Gali Janardhana Reddy said the party was ready to face him at the polls. “We are ready to face you. Let MLAs and MPs from the region resign and go to the polls. We will show our capabilities,” Reddy said. Reddy also launched a sharp attack on Nagendra questioning whether the BJP had asked him to transfer the money to hundreds of accounts. “Did we tell you to loot Rs 187 crore and send it to 600 accounts? Did we advise you to ensure Tukaram’s victory in the Lok Sabha election with that scam money? Did we ask you to send money to Mumbai, Telangana and Andhra Pradesh?” he asked. --IANS

“You are not in control.

Your karma has caught up with you,” he said.
